text: I was diagnosed with stage 4,  HER2-positive, invasive ductal
carcinoma of the left breast.
HER2-positive breast cancer is  a subtype of breast cancer that
we've learned is  very different.
They do tend to grow  a little quicker.
They do tend to recur more.
I was devastated.
I didn't know what that meant for my future.
I was scared that it was going  to change the dreams that I had
for my life.
Decades ago, before we had the  very specific treatments for
HER2 breast cancers,
women did not do well.
But now we've been able to  develop medications that
are very targeted.
Being a speaker at the Cancer Survivors event,
I was able to connect with a lot of amazing people,
who I've been able to  gain friendships with.
So I'm very honored and blessed  to have had the team that I
had at Sharp.
Havyne's just  a real inspiration.
She's just amazing.
I think the most important  thing that was so special about
her was maintaining a  real positive attitude.
I don't want people to think  that because you have a cancer
diagnosis that your life  is over,
that joy is gone,
and that you can't  have fun anymore.
That is the absolute opposite.
So fun and joy and positivity saved my life.
